newsitem.title: UK: British Queen's India visit still under discussion.
newsitem.headline: British Queen's India visit still under discussion.

text.p: Britain said on Monday that details were still being finalised for Queen Elizabeth's forthcoming visit to India, made controversial by plans to include the site of a massacre in 1919.
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kujmar Gujral said in an interview published on Sunday he wanted the British monarch to avoid the city of Amritsar to avoid bitterness over the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
"We are still discussing the details of the Queen's programme (with New Delhi)," a Foreign Office spokesman said.
British troops killed 379 unarmed demonstrators herded into a square in Amritsar in one of the most notorious incidents in the history of the British empire.
"It is a goodwill visit and we would not like to add anything historically that would cause bitterness," Gujral told the British newspaper The Observer.
"We have suggested as a government to the British a few days back that it would be much better if she doesn't visit Amritsar."
British officials, however, said Gujral's remarks did not accord completely with what London had previously understood to be Delhi's position. Britain was therefore seeking clarification.
The Queen had been due to go to Amritsar to visit the Sikh Golden Temple in the Punjabi city as part of a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the end of British imperial rule in the subcontinent.
